answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, with each walk’s voting influence discounted by its transition probability. A sybil cluster S connected to the honest graph by few edges has low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,V∖S)/vol(S), limiting trust flow across its boundary. With anchored trust, bounded walk length, and capped node influence, this bottleneck bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight; raven, lotus, and pulse attestations receive no extra weight merely by multiplying identities.
